fps.name: Shooters (FPS / battle royale)
fps.ph: Example: take every fight from cover
fps.review: Rewatch one death: where should you have been?

drills.name: Tracking
steps: Pick a smooth tracking scenario (Strafetrack, Smoothbot, or a moving bot in your game's range).
Keep your crosshair on the target's center. Move with your arm for big motions and your wrist for small ones.
Do 3 rounds. On each one, try to stay on target longer than the last.
drills.tip: Relax your grip. A tense hand makes tracking shaky.

drills.name: Recoil control
steps: Go to the practice range with your main gun.
Spray a full mag at a wall from medium range and look at the bullet pattern.
Spray again, pulling your mouse the opposite way of the pattern. Then try it on a moving target.
drills.tip: Learn one gun really well before moving to the next.

drills.name: Flicks
steps: Pick a flick scenario like Gridshot.
Do your first 2 runs slow. Only click when your crosshair is on the target.
Speed up on the next runs, but stop speeding up if accuracy drops below about 85%.
drills.tip: Accuracy first, speed second. Speed comes on its own.

drills.name: Target switching
steps: Pick a scenario with several targets on screen.
Move to the next target, settle, then shoot. Don't shoot while still moving.
Try to cut the pause between targets a little each round.
drills.tip: In real fights, switch to the weakest enemy first.

drills.name: Aim while moving
steps: In the range, strafe left and right while shooting a target.
Keep your crosshair on the target while your body moves.
In tactical shooters, practice stopping fully (counter-strafing) right before you shoot.
drills.tip: Good movement makes you harder to hit. Good aim makes it count.

drills.name: Crosshair placement
steps: Load a map in practice mode.
Walk through it with your crosshair always at head height.
Aim where an enemy would appear around each corner before you peek.
drills.tip: Good placement means you barely need to flick.

drills.name: Building and editing
steps: Load a creative map made for practicing builds and edits.
Repeat one build (like a 90 or a box) 20 times, slowly at first.
Practice the same edits from both sides until you don't have to think about the keys.
drills.tip: Mostly for Fortnite. Clean and steady beats fast and sloppy.

drills.name: Positioning
steps: Watch 3 of your deaths from today's games.
For each one, ask: was I in the open, or fighting more than one enemy at once?
Write one rule for next game, like "Always have cover within 2 steps."
drills.tip: Most fights are won before the first shot, by where you're standing.

moba.name: MOBA (League, Dota, Smite)
moba.ph: Example: check the minimap after every wave
moba.review: Rewatch one death: was the enemy jungler on the map?
moba.warm: Last-hitting in the practice tool, 10 min

drills.name: Last hitting
steps: Open the practice tool (League) or demo mode (Dota) with your main character.
Last hit minions for 10 minutes with no items that help farming.
Write down your number at 10 minutes and try to beat it next time.
drills.tip: Watch the minion health bars, not your character.

drills.name: Map awareness
steps: Play a game where you glance at the minimap every 3 to 5 seconds.
Each time an enemy goes missing, ask where they could be going.
Ping or play safe when 2 or more enemies are missing.
drills.tip: Most deaths come from an enemy you forgot about.

drills.name: Wave management
steps: Watch a short guide on freezing, slow pushing, and fast pushing.
In your next game, pick one wave plan before every back.
Notice how the wave you leave behind changes what happens next.
drills.tip: Leave a big wave crashing into the enemy tower before you back.

drills.name: Vision and wards
steps: Buy and place a ward every time you back.
Ward the paths the enemy uses to reach you, not just the middle of the river.
Clear enemy wards before objectives like dragon or Roshan.
drills.tip: Vision wins objectives.

drills.name: Small character pool
steps: Pick 2 or 3 characters for your role and only play those this week.
Learn their combos, power spikes, and best items.
Read up on one hard matchup each day.
drills.tip: Mastering a few beats knowing a little about all of them.

fighting.name: Fighting games (SF6, Tekken, Smash)
fighting.review: Rewatch one loss: what did they keep doing to you?
fighting.warm: Your main combo 10 times on each side

drills.name: Combo practice
steps: In training mode, pick one combo you can use in real matches.
Do it 10 times in a row without dropping it, on both sides of the screen.
Once it's easy, practice starting it from a real hit, like a punish or a counter hit.
drills.tip: One combo you never drop beats five you sometimes land.

drills.name: Anti-airs
steps: Set the training dummy to jump at you at random times.
React with your best anti-air every time.
Count how many you hit out of 20.
drills.tip: If they keep jumping in, make them pay.

drills.name: Punishing
steps: Record the dummy doing a move that's unsafe when you block it.
Block it, then punish with your best fast attack or combo.
Repeat for the 3 moves you lose to most.
drills.tip: Learning what's punishable is free damage.

drills.name: Defense
steps: Record the dummy doing a mix of high, low, and throw attacks.
Play it back on random and try to block or tech everything.
Notice which one gets you most, and practice that one.
drills.tip: Calm defense makes opponents run out of ideas.

drills.name: Matchup study
steps: Pick the character you lose to most.
Look up their most annoying moves and how to beat them.
Try each answer in training mode with that character as the dummy.
drills.tip: Knowing what's coming turns panic into a plan.

chess.name: Chess
chess.ph: Example: check every capture and check before I move
chess.review: Analyze one loss: find the move where it went wrong

drills.name: Tactics puzzles
steps: Do puzzles on Chess.com or Lichess (Lichess is free).
Before moving, look at every check, capture, and threat.
If you get one wrong, replay the answer and figure out why it works.
drills.tip: Accuracy beats speed. Take your time on each puzzle.

drills.name: Openings
steps: Pick one opening as White and one answer to 1.e4 and to 1.d4 as Black.
Learn the first 5 to 8 moves and the ideas behind them, not just the order.
Play a few games using only those openings.
drills.tip: Learn the plans, not just the moves.

drills.name: Endgames
steps: Practice basic checkmates: king and queen, then king and rook, against the computer.
Learn king and pawn endgames, like opposition and the square rule.
Then learn the two key rook endgames: the Lucena and Philidor positions.
drills.tip: Many games are won or lost in the endgame.

drills.name: Analyze your games
steps: Pick a recent game you lost.
Go through it yourself first and mark the moves you're unsure about.
Then check with the engine and write down your biggest mistake.
drills.tip: Your own games are your best teacher.

drills.name: Slower games
steps: Play 1 or 2 rapid games (15+10 or longer) instead of lots of blitz.
Use your time to check for blunders before every move.
Analyze them right after.
drills.tip: Slow games build habits. Fast games test them.

geo.name: GeoGuessr and geography
geo.ph: Example: check road lines and bollards before guessing
geo.review: Look at one bad round: what clue did you miss?

drills.name: Country clues
steps: Pick one region, like South America or Eastern Europe.
Study its clues: which side of the road they drive on, road line colors, bollards, signs, and license plates.
Use a study site like Plonk It, then play a map of only that region.
drills.tip: Learn one region well before moving on.

drills.name: Languages and scripts
steps: Learn to tell similar alphabets apart, like Thai vs Lao, or Cyrillic in Russia vs Ukraine vs Bulgaria.
Learn a few common letters or words for each.
Test yourself with screenshots of signs.
drills.tip: Special letters (like Ukrainian ї or Polish ł) often give the country away.

drills.name: Sun and landscape
steps: Learn the sun rule: in the Southern Hemisphere, the sun is in the north at midday.
Notice soil color, plants, and the type of houses.
Use these to narrow down the area before picking a country.
drills.tip: Narrow it down first, then guess.

drills.name: Map knowledge
steps: Learn where major cities and regions are inside big countries like the US, Brazil, and Russia.
Play a city or flag quiz (like Seterra) for one country.
Practice clicking closer to the right spot, not just the right country.
drills.tip: Getting the region right adds a lot of points.

drills.name: Timed rounds
steps: Play a few games with a short time limit.
Make a fast guess from the first clue you see.
Compare with your untimed scores.
drills.tip: Duels reward fast, confident guesses.

rts.name: Strategy games (RTS, 4X)
rts.review: Watch one replay: when did you have too many resources banked?
rts.warm: Your build order vs the AI

drills.name: Build orders
steps: Pick one standard build order for your faction or civ.
Play it against an easy AI until you can do it without looking it up.
Check your timing against a benchmark from a guide.
drills.tip: A clean opening makes the rest of the game easier.

drills.name: Hotkeys and control groups
steps: Learn the hotkeys for your most used buildings and units.
Put your army and production buildings on control groups.
Play a game using no mouse clicks on the bottom menu.
drills.tip: Fast hands come from good habits, not clicking faster.

drills.name: Macro cycle
steps: Keep making workers or villagers the whole game.
Every few seconds, spend your resources on units, buildings, or upgrades.
Avoid getting supply or population blocked.
drills.tip: Most ranked games are won by better economy.

drills.name: Scouting
steps: Send a scout early in every game.
Look for what the enemy is building and how fast they're expanding.
Change your plan based on what you see.
drills.tip: Knowing what's coming lets you counter it.

drills.name: Replay review
steps: Watch one of your losses at 2x speed.
Look for idle production, big piles of unspent resources, and lost fights.
Write one fix for next game.
drills.tip: Replays show what you couldn't see while playing.

card.name: Card games (Hearthstone, MTG, Clash Royale)
card.ph: Example: think about my opponent's next turn before I play
card.review: Look at one loss: which turn did you lose it?
card.warm: A couple of unranked games with your main deck

drills.name: Main deck mastery
steps: Pick one strong deck and stick with it for a week.
Learn every card in it and why it's there.
Write down which matchups feel easy and which feel hard.
drills.tip: Knowing one deck deeply beats switching every day.

drills.name: Mulligans and openings
steps: Look up which cards to keep in your opening hand for your deck.
Each game, decide your keep based on who you're playing against.
Plan your first 3 turns before you play turn 1.
drills.tip: A good start wins a lot of games.

drills.name: Tracking resources
steps: Keep track of what your opponent has played and what they could still have.
In Clash Royale, count elixir and track their 4-card cycle.
Use it to guess when they can't answer your play.
drills.tip: Playing around what's left is a big skill jump.

drills.name: Matchup study
steps: Pick the deck you lose to most.
Look up its key cards and its game plan.
Decide what you need to save your answers for.
drills.tip: Know their win condition and stop it.

drills.name: Slow turns
steps: Before each turn, list your possible plays.
Think one turn ahead: what will they do next?
Pick the play that leaves you safest, not just the flashiest.
drills.tip: Most losses come from rushing a turn.

roguelike.name: Roguelikes (Balatro, Hades, Slay the Spire)
roguelike.ph: Example: pick a build plan by floor 2
roguelike.review: Write down why your last run ended

drills.name: One build at a time
steps: Pick one character or strategy to focus on.
Play several runs trying to build around it.
Notice which items or cards make it work.
drills.tip: Learn what makes a build strong before mixing ideas.

drills.name: Run notes
steps: After each run, write down where and why it ended.
Look for patterns, like the same boss or the same mistake.
Plan one change for the next run.
drills.tip: Every run teaches something if you write it down.

drills.name: Boss and enemy patterns
steps: Pick the boss or enemy that ends most of your runs.
Watch a short guide or a top player beat it.
Practice its attack patterns on your next runs.
drills.tip: Patterns become easy once you know them.

drills.name: Watch a top player
steps: Watch one full run from a top player.
Pause at each big choice and guess what they'll pick.
Note the choices that surprise you.
drills.tip: Their decisions teach more than their mechanics.

rocket.name: Rocket League
rocket.ph: Example: rotate back post every time
rocket.review: Rewatch one goal against you: where should you have been?

drills.name: Free play car control
steps: Go into free play and hit the ball around without stopping.
Practice powersliding, half-flips, and landing on your wheels.
Try to keep the ball close to you for longer each time.
drills.tip: Car control is the base of every other skill.

drills.name: Aerials
steps: Load a beginner aerial training pack.
Jump, tilt back, and boost toward the ball. Feather your boost.
Move to harder packs once you hit most shots.
drills.tip: Start low and slow. Height comes with practice.

drills.name: Rotation
steps: After you hit the ball, rotate out to your back post.
Don't go for the ball if a teammate is closer.
Watch a short rotation guide if this is new to you.
drills.tip: Good rotation wins more games than flashy mechanics.

drills.name: Kickoffs
steps: Practice speed flip or fast kickoffs from every spawn.
Hit the ball with the front of your car, aiming slightly to the side.
Do 10 from each spot.
drills.tip: Winning kickoffs gives you a free head start.

drills.name: Saves and defense
steps: Load a goalie training pack.
Stay in net and face the ball. Don't jump too early.
Practice clearing the ball to the side, not the middle.
drills.tip: Patience in net saves more goals than flashy plays.

racing.name: Racing (Forza, Gran Turismo, Mario Kart)
racing.ph: Example: brake in a straight line before turning
racing.review: Watch one lap replay: where did you lose the most time?
racing.warm: 5 warm-up laps on your main track

drills.name: Racing line
steps: Turn on the racing line helper if your game has one.
Go wide into the turn, cut to the inside at the apex, then drift wide on the way out.
Do laps until you hit the same line every time.
drills.tip: A clean line is faster than a wild one.

drills.name: Braking points
steps: Pick a marker, like a sign or board, for each corner.
Brake hard in a straight line at that marker.
Move the marker a little later each lap until you miss the corner, then back off.
drills.tip: Most time is found in braking.

drills.name: Time trials
steps: Run time trials against your own ghost.
Focus on one corner at a time.
Write down your best lap.
drills.tip: Beating your own ghost shows real progress.

drills.name: Consistency
steps: Try to do 10 laps in a row with no mistakes.
Drive at about 95% speed instead of 100%.
Count how many clean laps you get.
drills.tip: Races are won by fewest mistakes.

drills.name: Drifts and shortcuts
steps: For kart racers, practice drift boosts on every turn.
Learn one shortcut on your favorite track.
Practice holding items to block attacks from behind.
drills.tip: Mostly for Mario Kart and other kart racers.

sports.name: Sports games (EA FC, NBA 2K, Madden)
sports.review: Rewatch one score against you: what went wrong?
sports.warm: Skill games or practice mode, 10 min

drills.name: Skill moves
steps: Go to the practice arena or skill games.
Learn 2 or 3 moves that work well, and practice them until they're automatic.
Use them in real games only when you have space.
drills.tip: A few reliable moves beat a dozen you fumble.

drills.name: Defense
steps: Play one game focusing only on defense.
Stay between your opponent and the goal or basket. Don't rush in.
Switch players smartly instead of chasing with one.
drills.tip: Patient defense makes your opponent make mistakes.

drills.name: Plays and tactics
steps: Learn 3 plays or a formation that works for you.
Practice them in practice mode.
Use them on purpose in your next games.
drills.tip: Having a plan beats making it up every time.

drills.name: Watch the real sport
steps: Watch a real game or highlights.
Notice how real teams pass, space out, and defend.
Try one of those ideas in your next game.
drills.tip: Real-life tactics often work in the game too.

rhythm.name: Rhythm games (osu!, Beat Saber, Guitar Hero)
rhythm.ph: Example: aim for accuracy, not just passing
rhythm.review: Replay the section you failed most
rhythm.warm: A few easy songs to warm up

drills.name: Warm-up songs
steps: Play 2 or 3 songs a bit below your level.
Focus on smooth, relaxed movement.
Don't push for scores yet.
drills.tip: Warm hands play better than cold ones.

drills.name: Accuracy practice
steps: Pick a song you can pass but not full combo.
Slow it down if your game allows it, or play an easier version.
Aim for perfect timing on every note before speeding up.
drills.tip: Accuracy at slow speed turns into accuracy at full speed.

drills.name: Hard sections
steps: Find the part of a song you always fail.
Practice just that part (use practice mode or a loop if there is one).
Play the full song again once it feels better.
drills.tip: Practice the hard part, not the whole song over and over.

drills.name: Stamina
steps: Play songs with long, steady note streams.
Start shorter, then go a little longer each week.
Stop if your hands or arms hurt.
drills.tip: Build up slowly. Rest days help too.

action.name: Action and platformers (Souls, Celeste, Geometry Dash)
action.ph: Example: learn the boss's moves before attacking
action.review: Write down where you died most today
action.warm: Replay a part you've already beaten

drills.name: Practice hard parts
steps: Find the part you die on most.
Use practice mode, checkpoints, or save states to repeat just that part.
Once you beat it 3 times in a row, try it in a full run.
drills.tip: Repeating a short section is faster than restarting the whole level.

drills.name: Boss patterns
steps: Fight the boss just to learn its moves, not to win.
Notice the warning sign (tell) before each attack.
Learn when it's safe to attack and when to dodge.
drills.tip: Patience beats greed. Get one hit in, then back off.

drills.name: Movement tech
steps: Learn one advanced move your game has, like a dash cancel or a wall jump.
Practice it somewhere easy and safe.
Use it in real levels.
drills.tip: Movement tech makes everything else easier.

drills.name: Full runs
steps: Do a full run or a long stretch without stopping.
Note where you lost the most time or lives.
Practice those parts next session.
drills.tip: Full runs test whether your practice actually stuck.

puzzle.name: Puzzle games (Tetris, puzzle battles)
puzzle.review: Watch one replay: where did your stack get messy?

drills.name: Finesse
steps: Learn the fastest key presses to place each piece (called finesse).
Practice slowly with a finesse trainer if your game has one.
Speed up only once you make few mistakes.
drills.tip: Fewer key presses means faster play.

drills.name: Clean stacking
steps: Play a few games focused only on keeping your stack flat.
Avoid leaving holes.
Leave one column open for line clears.
drills.tip: A clean stack gives you more choices.

drills.name: T-spins and attacks
steps: Learn one T-spin setup.
Practice it in free play until you can do it without thinking.
Use it in real games when it fits naturally.
drills.tip: Learn one setup at a time.

drills.name: Sprint practice
steps: Play a few 40-line sprints.
Write down your best time.
Try to beat it next session.
drills.tip: Steady speed beats rushed speed.

mmo.name: MMO and RPG (WoW, FFXIV, Genshin)
mmo.ph: Example: learn my rotation before the next raid
mmo.review: Look at one wipe or fail: what mechanic got you?
mmo.warm: Rotation on a target dummy, 10 min

drills.name: Rotation
steps: Look up the basic rotation or combo for your class or character.
Practice it on a target dummy until it feels natural.
Track your damage and try to raise it.
drills.tip: Smooth beats fast. Don't drop your main skills.

drills.name: Mechanics
steps: Before a dungeon or raid, watch a short guide on its bosses.
Learn what each warning or attack means.
Focus on surviving first. Damage comes later.
drills.tip: Staying alive does more damage than dying.

drills.name: Keybinds and UI
steps: Move your most used skills to keys that are easy to reach.
Set up your screen so you can see warnings and enemy attacks.
Practice the new layout on a target dummy.
drills.tip: Good setup makes hard fights easier.

drills.name: Gear and builds
steps: Look up a good build guide for your class or character.
Compare your gear and stats to it.
Pick one upgrade to work toward.
drills.tip: Small upgrades add up.

sandbox.name: Minecraft and sandbox
sandbox.review: Think about your last loss: what would you change?
sandbox.warm: Bridging or a quick warm-up game

drills.name: Bridging
steps: Practice speed-bridging on a practice server or in creative.
Start with simple bridging, then try faster methods.
Time yourself across the same distance.
drills.tip: Mostly for Bedwars and other PvP modes.

drills.name: PvP combos
steps: Practice hitting while strafing left and right.
Learn to tap forward between hits to keep combos going.
Practice on a duel server against friends or bots.
drills.tip: Steady movement wins more fights than fast clicking.

drills.name: Building practice
steps: Pick one building idea, like a house or a bridge.
Use depth, mixed blocks, and a nice roof shape.
Compare it to builds you like and note what's different.
drills.tip: Copying great builds is a great way to learn.

drills.name: Learn one mechanic
steps: Pick one thing to learn, like redstone basics or an efficient farm.
Follow a short tutorial.
Build it yourself without looking.
drills.tip: Build it once from memory and it sticks.

general.name: Other games
general.ph: Example: focus on one thing to improve today
general.review: Think about one loss: what would you do differently?

drills.name: Practice your weakest skill
steps: Pick the one skill that loses you the most games.
Find a way to practice just that part, like a practice mode or an easy match.
Do it for 15 minutes without worrying about winning.
drills.tip: Focused practice beats just playing more.

drills.name: Review your games
steps: Watch a replay or think back on a recent loss.
Find the moment it went wrong.
Write one fix for next time.
drills.tip: Mistakes are only wasted if you don't learn from them.

drills.name: Learn from a top player
steps: Watch a top player or a guide for your game.
Pause at big decisions and guess what they'll do.
Try one of their ideas in your next game.
drills.tip: Copy what they do, then understand why.

drills.name: Try one new strategy
steps: Pick one new strategy, character, or build.
Play a few games with it.
Keep what works and drop what doesn't.
drills.tip: Trying new things keeps you from getting stuck.

PROJECTS: The computer picks a number from 1 to 100. Tell the player higher or lower.
Ask how long the password should be, then print a random one with letters, numbers, and symbols.
Play against the computer. Keep score until someone gets to 3.
Roll any dice the user asks for, like 2d6, and show each roll and the total.
Add, list, and remove tasks. Save them to a text file so they stay.
Convert between miles and km, pounds and kg, and F and C.
Ask 5 questions from a list, check the answers, and show a final score.
Move files in a folder into subfolders by type (images, docs, zips).
Read a text file and print the 10 most used words.
Pick a random word and let the player guess letters, with 6 lives.
Add spending to a CSV file and print the total for each category.
Ask for minutes and count down in the terminal, then print a message.
Ask for kills and deaths from your last 10 games and print your K/D and best game.
Store a list of characters and randomly pick a full squad for you and your friends.
A box turns green at a random time. Click as fast as you can and show your time.
Count how many clicks you can do in 5 seconds.
Start, stop, and reset buttons with minutes, seconds, and milliseconds.
Show a new quote every time a button is clicked.
Enter a bill and tip percent, then show the tip and total.
Two players on one screen. Show who wins or if it's a tie.
Show 5 random colors with their hex codes. Click one to copy it.
